title: Moments (maths mechanics)
examples: How do I find the reaction force at the pivot point?
What is the difference between a moment and a force?
Can you show me an example with three supports?

explain.say: Today we learn about moments and equilibrium of rods. A moment is a turning effect caused by a force. We measure it in Newton metres.
For a rod to be in equilibrium, the sum of all clockwise moments must equal the sum of all anti-clockwise moments. This is the first condition.

draw.text: Sum CW Moments = Sum ACW Moments

explain.say: We also know that the sum of all vertical forces acting on the rod must equal zero. This is the second condition for balance.
Consider a beam supported at two points, A and B. We take moments about point A to find the reaction force at B. This is the tilting point method.

items: Consider beam supported at A and B

explain.say: If we take moments about point A, the moment caused by the reaction force at A is zero. So we only balance the other forces.

faq.a: A moment is the turning effect. It depends on the force and how far away the force is from the pivot point.
asks: How do I calculate a moment?

faq.q: Why do I have to balance the moments?
faq.a: If the moments are not balanced, the rod will rotate or accelerate. Equilibrium means it is perfectly still.
asks: What does equilibrium mean for a beam?
Why must the turning effects cancel out?

faq.q: How do I find the reaction force at a support?
faq.a: You must use the two conditions: sum of forces is zero, and sum of moments is zero. You take moments about one support.
asks: What is the best point to take moments about?
Do I need to use both force and moment equations?

faq.q: What if the rod is supported by three points?
faq.a: You will have three unknown reaction forces. You must use the three equations: sum of forces in x, sum of forces in y, and sum of moments.
asks: How many equations do I need for three supports?
Does the number of supports change the method?

faq.q: If I take moments about a support, why does that force disappear?
faq.a: Because the force acts directly through the pivot point. The perpendicular distance is zero, so the moment is zero.
asks: Why is the moment zero at the pivot?
Does the reaction force at the pivot cause a moment?

facts: A moment is calculated by multiplying a force by its perpendicular distance from the pivot.
For a body to be in equilibrium, the sum of all clockwise moments must equal the sum of all anti-clockwise moments.
The sum of all vertical forces acting on a horizontal rod must equal zero.
When taking moments about a support, the reaction force at that support causes zero moment.

quiz.say: A beam has a 10 Newton force acting 2 metres from the pivot. The resulting moment is:
quiz.why: The moment is the force multiplied by the perpendicular distance, so 10 times 2 is 20 Newton metres.

wrong.0: This incorrectly divides the force by the distance.
wrong.1: This forgets to include the unit of distance in the calculation.
wrong.3: This incorrectly adds the force and the distance together.

quiz.say: If the sum of clockwise moments is 30 Nm, the sum of anti-clockwise moments must be:
quiz.why: For the rod to be in equilibrium, the turning effects must balance each other out completely.

wrong.0: This incorrectly adds the two sums together.
wrong.1: This incorrectly divides the two sums by two.
wrong.2: This assumes that the total moment must always be zero regardless of the forces.

quiz.say: A beam is supported at A and B. If we take moments about A, the moment from the reaction force at A is:
quiz.why: Because the force acts directly through the pivot point A, the perpendicular distance is zero, making the moment zero.

wrong.0: This incorrectly treats the reaction force as if it were acting at a distance.
wrong.1: This confuses the reaction force with the distance between the supports.
wrong.2: This brings in an irrelevant force that is not part of the moment calculation about A.
